title: Oracle is putting a Quantinuum quantum computer inside its own data centre
excerpt: Quantinuum's Helios machine will be physically deployed in a US Oracle Cloud data centre, with a preview service due in coming months.
content_html:
Oracle and Quantinuum have agreed a multi-year partnership under which Quantinuum will physically install its Helios quantum computer inside a US Oracle Cloud Infrastructure AI data centre, and Oracle will sell access to it as a managed OCI service.

No financial terms were disclosed, no launch customer was named, and no firm date was given beyond a preview “in the coming months”.

Most quantum cloud offerings are brokerage: a customer sends a job from a hyperscaler’s console to a machine sitting in the quantum vendor’s own facility, and the results come back.

Putting Helios inside an OCI data centre puts the quantum processor on the same fabric as Oracle’s GPUs and HPC capacity, under the same governance and security controls, which is what makes hybrid workloads, the ones that hand a problem back and forth between classical and quantum hardware, worth attempting at all.

Helios is not new hardware. Quantinuum launched it commercially in November 2025: a trapped-ion machine with 98 physical qubits, 48 demonstrated logical qubits, and an average two-qubit gate fidelity of 99.921%.

Its power draw is roughly 60kW, against the tens of megawatts a leading classical supercomputer consumes, though that comparison flatters the machine considerably given how narrow the set of problems it can currently address remains.

“Deploying Helios inside OCI gives Quantinuum and Oracle an opportunity to create a unique deeply integrated environment for hybrid workloads, explore enterprise use cases with customers, and accelerate commercial adoption,” said Rajeeb Hazra, Quantinuum’s president and chief executive.

Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice-president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, was more careful about what is on offer.

The goal, he said, is to give developers “a practical and secure way to explore how quantum computing could complement their existing AI and HPC workloads on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure while improving compute efficiency and energy use”.

The named target workloads are the usual list: drug discovery, materials science, financial modelling, and large-scale optimisation in logistics and energy.

Oracle is arriving late. AWS has offered Braket since August 2020, Microsoft’s Azure Quantum has been generally available since February 2022 and already carries Quantinuum’s own H-series hardware, and IBM has sold access to its own machines since 2016.

Oracle’s differentiator is not breadth but depth: one vendor, one machine, physically present, rather than a marketplace of remote QPUs. Whether enterprises want that trade is the thing the preview will establish.

Nvidia is absent from the announcement, despite Quantinuum having an existing NVQLink integration dating to last November, and despite Oracle’s hybrid pitch resting on GPU proximity.

For Quantinuum, the deal is the second significant validation of a year that has already reshaped the company.

It priced its Nasdaq IPO in June at $60 a share, selling 28 million Class A shares to raise $1.68bn at a valuation of roughly $14bn, above its own upsized range and more than twenty times oversubscribed, on revenue of $30.9m and a net loss of $192.6m for 2025.

It trades as QNT. Its roadmap runs to Sol in 2027 and Apollo, the machine it says will demonstrate genuine quantum advantage, in 2029.

Europe has been building in a different direction. Finland’s IQM has put superconducting machines directly into research data centres rather than routing access through a hyperscaler, on the argument that co-location with classical HPC is where useful work will first appear.

Oracle’s arrangement borrows that logic and applies it to a commercial cloud, which is either the sensible synthesis or a way of catching up quickly, depending on how generous you are feeling.

Investors were unmoved as Oracle closed down 3.69% at $145.48 on Tuesday and Quantinuum slipped 0.94% to $56.06, recovering slightly after hours.

A partnership with no disclosed terms, no named customer, and no launch date is difficult to price, which is roughly the position quantum computing has occupied for a decade.

What none of the parties has offered is a workload that runs better this way today. The release leans on the phrase “explore enterprise use cases with customers”, which is the industry’s standard construction for work that has not yet produced a result.

Quantinuum’s own $30.9m of annual revenue against a $192.6m loss is a reasonable proxy for how much commercial quantum computing currently exists anywhere.

content_html_zh:
Oracle 和 Quantinuum 已达成多年合作伙伴关系，根据该合作关系，Quantinuum 将在美国 Oracle 云基础设施 AI 数据中心内实际安装其 Helios 量子计算机，而 Oracle 将作为托管 OCI 服务出售其访问权限。

没有披露任何财务条款，没有指定启动客户，也没有给出除了“未来几个月”预览之外的确定日期。

大多数量子云产品都是经纪服务：客户将作业从超大规模企业的控制台发送到量子供应商自己设施中的机器，然后返回结果。

将 Helios 放入 OCI 数据中心内，可以将量子处理器置于与 Oracle GPU 和 HPC 容量相同的结构上，处于相同的治理和安全控制之下，这使得混合工作负载（在经典硬件和量子硬件之间来回处理问题的工作负载）值得尝试。

Helios 并不是新硬件。 Quantinuum 于 2025 年 11 月将其商业化：一台俘获离子机器，拥有 98 个物理量子位、48 个演示逻辑量子位，平均两个量子位门保真度为 99.921%。

它的功耗约为 60kW，而领先的经典超级计算机的功耗则为数十兆瓦，不过考虑到它目前能解决的问题范围仍然很窄，这种比较让这台机器显得相当讨人喜欢。

Quantinuum 总裁兼首席执行官 Rajeeb Hazra 表示：“在 OCI 内部署 Helios 使 Quantinuum 和 Oracle 有机会为混合工作负载创建独特的深度集成环境、与客户一起探索企业用例并加速商业采用。”

Oracle 云基础设施执行副总裁 Mahesh Thiagarajan 对所提供的服务更加谨慎。

他说，目标是为开发人员提供“一种实用且安全的方式来探索量子计算如何补充 Oracle 云基础设施上现有的 AI 和 HPC 工作负载，同时提高计算效率和能源使用”。

指定的目标工作负载是通常的列表：药物发现、材料科学、财务建模以及物流和能源的大规模优化。

甲骨文迟到了。 AWS 自 2020 年 8 月起提供 Braket，微软的 Azure Quantum 自 2022 年 2 月起全面上市，并已搭载 Quantinuum 自己的 H 系列硬件，IBM 自 2016 年起出售自己机器的访问权限。

Oracle 的优势不在于广度，而在于深度：一个供应商、一台机器、物理存在，而不是远程 QPU 市场。 企业是否想要这种贸易是预览将确定的事情。

尽管 Quantinuum 早在去年 11 月就已集成了 NVQLink，而且 Oracle 的混合方案也依赖于 GPU 的邻近性，但 Nvidia 并未出现在此次公告中。

对于 Quantinuum 来说，这笔交易是该公司今年重塑的第二次重大验证。

该公司 6 月份在纳斯达克的 IPO 定价为每股 60 美元，出售 2800 万股 A 类股票，筹集 16.8 亿美元，估值约为 140 亿美元，高于其自己的上限，超额认购超过 20 倍，营收为 3090 万美元，2025 年净亏损为 1.926 亿美元。

它的交易名称为 QNT。 它的路线图是在 2027 年推出 Sol，并在 2029 年推出 Apollo，据称该机器将展示真正的量子优势。

欧洲一直在朝着不同的方向发展。 芬兰的 IQM 已将超导机器直接放入研究数据中心，而不是通过超大规模计算机进行路由访问，理由是与经典 HPC 共置是有用工作首先出现的地方。

甲骨文的安排借用了这种逻辑，并将其应用到商业云中，这要么是明智的综合，要么是一种快速追赶的方式，具体取决于你的慷慨程度。

投资者不为所动，甲骨文周二收盘下跌 3.69%，至 145.48 美元，Quantinuum 下跌 0.94%，至 56.06 美元，盘后小幅回升。

没有披露条款、没有指定客户、也没有发布日期的合作伙伴关系很难定价，这大致是量子计算十年来所占据的地位。

目前各方都没有提供以这种方式运行得更好的工作负载。 该版本的重点是“与客户一起探索企业用例”，这是针对尚未产生结果的工作的行业标准构建。

Quantinuum 的年收入为 3090 万美元，而亏损为 1.926 亿美元，这合理地反映了目前任何地方存在多少商业量子计算。
